steps.name: TMM normalization, n=1 count-model attempt, effect-size ranked gene list
caveats: 0 residual df: any p-value a tool emits here (e.g., DESeq2 falling back to prior-only dispersion) is an assumption stated as a statistic. Do not let it into the deliverable.
A single sample pair can be dominated by technical or batch noise; the top-changed list is a candidate list, not a validated finding. Downstream interpretation must not overclaim.
Condition values must be read from metadata.csv as-is; do not assume spelling or case of 'treated'/'control'.
If the gene-id column is not a recognizable ID space (Ensembl / Entrez / symbol), map via the provisioned UniProt human ID mapping (local file) rather than dropping genes silently.
Salmon length correction is undocumented per the profile; TMM normalization is used precisely because it is robust to this, but note the ambiguity in the methods note.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 x 3; layout expected as one gene-id column + 2 sample columns — verify) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows, one condition column; read the actual condition values, do not hardcode 'treated'/'control'). Organism: Homo sapiens; tissue: liver; design: 1 vs 1, no replication. The profile is silent on whether Salmon applied length correction; treat the matrix as raw counts.
steps.question: Which of the 12,000 genes in counts.csv show expression change between the treated and control liver samples, and what exactly happens when a standard count model is fit with 1 sample per condition?
constraints: Treat the matrix as raw integer counts. Verify integrality at ingestion; if values are non-integer (possible length-corrected salmon output), round, record the observation, and proceed.
Normalize with edgeR::calcNormFactors (TMM size factors) and report the size factors for both samples.

Attempt a standard count-model fit: DESeq2::DESeq with design ~ condition (or equivalent limma/edgeR GLM). Capture and verbatim record the exact error, warnings, and any messages produced. Expected: dispersion estimation fails or is prior-only given 0 residual df.

If the fit completes using prior-only dispersion, discard its p-values: they encode an assumed dispersion, not data. No p-value or FDR from this design may appear in any output as a significance call.
Deliverable 'change list' definition: genes with |log2FC| >= 1 AND total raw count across both samples >= 10. Also always output the top 50 genes by |log2FC| regardless of threshold.
Compute log2FC = log2(cpm with prior.count=0.5 in treated) - log2(cpm with prior.count=0.5 in control) using TMM-normalized cpm (edgeR::cpm(log=TRUE, prior.count=0.5)).

Outputs: (a) full 12,000-gene table with gene id, symbol where mappable (else the raw id), raw counts, TMM size factors, normalized cpm per sample, log2FC, abs(log2FC), rank by |log2FC|; (b) the thresholded change list plus top-50-by-rank list; (c) a short methods note stating 0 residual df, the exact count-model behavior observed, and why no p-values/FDR are reported.
acceptance_criteria: TMM-normalized 12,000 x 2 count table produced with both size factors reported.
Per-gene log2FC table covering all 12,000 genes, ranked by |log2FC|.
The attempted count-model DE fit's exact behavior (error text or warnings) is recorded verbatim in the methods note.
The change list is defined solely by |log2FC| >= 1 plus total count >= 10, and every output artifact labels it as not significance-tested.
No p-value or FDR column is presented as a significance call anywhere in the outputs.

steps.name: Pathway context for top-changed genes (human WikiPathways ORE)
caveats: Hypergeometric p-values here measure overlap of a magnitude-ranked list with a pathway — conflating them with DE significance would be a category error; keep the framing strict in all output text.
The WikiPathways GMT uses HGNC symbols; if mapping fails, check whether the ids are Ensembl and remap via org.Hs.eg.db rather than proceeding with unmapped ids.
Small input lists (the fallback top-100) yield noisy ORE; report list size so the reader can gauge stability.
steps.context: Input: T1S1's |log2FC| >= 1 change list (fallback: top 100 genes by |log2FC| if fewer than 15 genes pass the threshold — state which input was used). Reference data needed: a human pathway gene set collection — use the provisioned human WikiPathways GMT (HGNC symbols; organism matches Homo sapiens). Do NOT use the mouse or rat WikiPathways files. Symbol mapping must happen locally (no network): org.Hs.eg.db for Ensembl/Entrez -> SYMBOL; if ids are already symbols, use as-is; otherwise the provisioned UniProt human ID mapping as fallback.
steps.question: Which human pathways are over-represented among the top-changed genes between treated and control liver, as exploratory context for a not-significance-tested change list?
constraints: Use only the human WikiPathways GMT; the mouse and rat GMTs are present in the reference store and must not be used on this human dataset.
Report the symbol-mapping success rate; drop unmapped ids and report the count.

Run over-representation (hypergeometric, e.g., clusterProfiler::enricher with GSEABase GMT loading) on the combined change list; additionally, if both the up- and down-regulated sublists contain >= 15 genes, run directional ORE on each.

Label all enrichment outputs as exploratory context for a not-significance-tested gene list. Do not present hypergeometric p-values as evidence that any gene is significantly differentially expressed.
acceptance_criteria: ORE result table (pathway, overlap, p, FDR) produced for the stated input list, with the input list size and definition printed alongside.
Symbol mapping rate reported, with >= 80% of input genes resolved to HGNC symbols (otherwise the id space must be re-examined and remapped before concluding).
Outputs explicitly framed as exploratory context, not a significance claim.

plan.title: n=1 liver treated-vs-control DE by effect size
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are 1 treated vs 1 control human liver bulk RNA-seq libraries (Salmon gene counts, 12,000 genes; counts.csv 12000x3, metadata.csv 2 samples with a condition column). With one sample per condition the design has 0 residual degrees of freedom: dispersion/variance cannot be estimated, so no p-value or FDR exists for this comparison — targeted literature search found no standard significance-testing method for this design, confirming that the defensible deliverable is an effect-size-based change list, clearly labeled as not significance-tested. The plan therefore: (1) normalizes with TMM, attempts a standard count-model DE fit to document its exact behavior under n=1 (discarding any p-values it might emit), and produces the per-gene log2FC table ranked by magnitude with a 2-fold threshold and low-count filter; (2) maps the top-changed genes to HGNC symbols and runs over-representation against the provisioned human WikiPathways sets for exploratory pathway context only. The treatment agent is not named in the context, so no external-validation or drug-target step is planned.

input.query: "no biological replicates" AND "differential expression" AND ("one sample per condition" OR "single sample per group") RNA-seq
differential expression analysis RNA-seq without biological replicates single sample per condition method
DESeq2 OR edgeR OR limma "one sample per condition" OR "single replicate" differential expression approach
